item.title: Narita Unagi Guide: Best Eel Restaurants & Access
item.description: The temple town of Narita is one of the best places near Tokyo to feast on unagi (freshwater eel) — a tradition stretching back centuries to feed pilgrims visiting Narita-san. Along the atmospheric Omotesando approach to the temple, dozens of long-established eel restaurants fillet, skewer and grill eel fresh to order, often in full view of the street, then glaze it in sweet-savoury tare sauce over rice as unadon or unaju.

item.title: Narita-san Shinshoji Temple Guide: Access from the Airport & Tips
item.description: Just minutes from Narita Airport, Narita-san Shinshoji Temple is one of the most important and atmospheric Buddhist temples in the Tokyo area — the perfect first or last stop on a trip to Japan. Founded in 940 and headquarters of the Shingon Chisan sect, it enshrines Fudo Myo-o, the fierce, flame-wreathed guardian deity, and draws millions of worshippers a year (it ranks among Japan’s busiest for New Year’s visits). Spread across a hillside of grand halls, a soaring pagoda and a tranquil landscaped park, and approached by a charming old street of eel restaurants and souvenir shops, it offers a deep dose of living Japanese tradition right by the airport.

item.title: Naritasan Calligraphy Guide: Shodo Experience & Access
item.description: The temple town of Narita is a wonderful place to try shodo (Japanese calligraphy) — the meditative art of writing characters with brush and ink. Narita-san is home to the Naritasan Calligraphy Museum, one of Japan’s leading museums devoted to the art, and the temple offers shakyo (sutra copying), where visitors trace or brush a Buddhist sutra in quiet concentration as a form of prayer and mindfulness. Hands-on brush workshops let you grind ink, learn the basic strokes and create your own piece to take home.

item.title: Naritasan Setsubun Guide: Bean-Throwing Festival & Access
item.description: Each February 3rd, Narita-san Shinshoji Temple hosts one of Japan’s most famous Setsubun celebrations — the bean-throwing ritual that drives out bad luck and welcomes spring. From a special stage, costumed participants hurl roasted soybeans (and lucky packets) to huge crowds shouting the traditional cry, and Narita-san is renowned for its celebrity guests: famous sumo grand champions, NHK taiga drama actors and other stars take part, drawing big crowds and national TV coverage.

item.title: Chiba Solo Travel Guide: From Narita Layovers to Boso Peninsula Exploration
item.description: Chiba suits solo travel well. Its public transport is good for the main routes, its food culture is built around single-person dining (fish market counters, unagi lunch sets, fishing port izakaya), and its most interesting experiences — temple walking, coastal cycling, a dawn fish market — are better done alone than in groups. For travellers arriving through Narita, it is also the most immediately accessible prefecture in Japan. Making the Most of a Narita Layover Narita Airport is in Chiba Prefecture, and the area around it offers one of the most accessible cultural experiences in Japan for travellers with time between flights.

item.title: Best Hotels & Ryokan in Chiba: Tokyo Disney, Narita & Boso Peninsula
item.description: Chiba Prefecture surrounds much of greater Tokyo and serves three very different traveller needs: Tokyo Disney Resort (the most-visited theme park in Asia), Narita Airport hotels (for transit and early-departure stays), and the Boso Peninsula (a dramatic Pacific coastline with fishing villages, flower fields, and surf beaches largely unknown to foreign visitors). Best Areas to Stay Maihama (Tokyo Disney Resort) The Disney area — Maihama Station is the gateway to Tokyo Disneyland and DisneySea.
